summary:
LaunchPad is an interactive space mission design game that puts players in the shoes of real mission teams, challenging them to turn ambitious scientific objectives into successful space missions. Players complete four missions (A Voyage to the ISS, PUNCH, Artemis 2, and Artemis 4), select spacecraft, choose scientific instruments, and amount of food, water, and fuel while managing competing constraints such as budget and mass. Every decision carries consequences, requiring the player to balance engineering trade-offs and adapt to unexpected challenges to achieve mission success.
Grounded in real-world space exploration, LaunchPad incorporates authentic NASA photographs, mission facts, and scientific information from International Space Station expeditions, the PUNCH mission, and Artemis II, alongside NASA renderings of the planned Artemis IV mission. By bringing actual missions and spacecraft into the gameplay, players can connect their decisions to the engineering and discoveries shaping space exploration today.
More than a game, LaunchPad aims to transform abstract aerospace concepts into an engaging, hands-on learning experience and inspire young people who might never have imagined a future in space exploration to see themselves as the scientists, engineers, and explorers who will shape humanity's future among the stars.
details:
LaunchPad is an interactive space mission design and simulation game that allows players to experience the challenges of planning and executing a real-world space mission. Rather than simply learning about aerospace engineering through textbooks or videos, players take on the roles of mission planners, engineers, scientists, and astronauts, making decisions that directly influence the outcome of their missions.

The game begins with players assembling an astronaut crew and selecting a scientific mission objective. Players must then make a series of engineering and strategic decisions, including choosing the proper spacecraft, scientific instrument selection, food, water, oxygen, and fuel. Throughout the process, they must balance competing resources such as budget and mass. Each decision introduces trade-offs: of course bringing backup instruments would be wise, but when it comes to space travel, every extra kilogram matters, not to mention that there may not be enough funding for backup instruments. Players, therefore, are forced to think critically, adapt their strategies in real time, and determine exactly how to get the most out of their available resources.

A central feature of LaunchPad is its usage of real-world space exploration. The game incorporates authentic NASA photographs, fun facts, and mission information from ISS expeditions, the PUNCH mission, and Artemis II, alongside NASA renderings for the planned Artemis IV mission. This connects the virtual experience to real scientific discoveries and ongoing exploration efforts, helping players understand that the engineering challenges they encounter are the same challenges faced by real mission teams.

LaunchPad also features eight real-life astronauts hailing from different nations and backgrounds. Each astronaut has unique strengths and limitations informed by their real-world experiences and professional expertise. Players have to consider their crew’s individual capabilities when it comes to assembling their mission team, introducing another layer of strategic decision-making while showcasing the international nature of space exploration 

LaunchPad also incorporates both mental and physical health metrics of the astronauts that mission control must carefully monitor. If either dips too low, the mission itself will be in jeopardy. Moreover, there is a relationship percentage to show how animus relationships have become on the trip. If relationship percentage dips too low, the astronauts will become far less efficient as they no longer will be working together effectively.

What truly sets LaunchPad apart is its ability to make complex aerospace concepts both accessible and engaging to young people with drastically different levels of engineering and scientific knowledge. By incorporating three different difficulty tiers for each level, LaunchPad allows children of all ages to explore NASA’s missions and tribulation. This then encourages experimentation, resource management, critical thinking, and problem-solving. Instead of merely explaining how designing mission plans involves extreme trade-offs, LaunchPad allows them to experience those trade-offs firsthand, learn from their mistakes, and try different approaches.

Creatively, Launchpad combines real NASA mission information, astronaut-based gameplay, educational simulation, and strategy gaming into one experience. We moved beyond traditional educational games that teach isolated scientific concepts and instead demonstrate how an entire space mission comes together. We balanced scientific accuracy with accessibility, ensuring that the game remains engaging and does not require expansive amounts of prior knowledge of engineering or science. This was achieved through having 3 different difficulty tiers for each level, allowing children of all ages to explore LaunchPad. We also ensured we represented the international diversity of the space community, showing players there is no single path, background, or role that leads into space exploration. All are welcome.

Ultimately, LaunchPad’s intended impact extends beyond teaching students how to design a space mission; it aims to empower young people who may have never considered themselves capable of contributing to space exploration to recognize that they have a place in its future. By placing them in control of their own missions, we hope to turn passive curiosity about the stars into the confidence needed to pursue the engineering, science, and discoveries that will take humanity there.
